newsitem.title: UK: UK refers P&0 /Stena ferry venture to MMC.
newsitem.headline: UK refers P&0 /Stena ferry venture to MMC.

text.p: The British government said on Thursday it would refer the proposed joint venture between shipping group Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co (P&O) and Swedish ferry operator Stena Line AB to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) for investigation.
The two companies unveiled plans in early October to join forces on three routes across the English Channel in an offensive against Eurotunnel SA/Plc's Channel Tunnel.

The planned merger was designed to rationalise the two shipping lines' capacity on the busy short-sea route where the English Channel is at its narrowest and competition with the channel tunnel most fierce.

The pair said at the time of launching the venture that they expected to be able to slash 75 million pounds off their combined fixed cost base of 280 million pounds, as well as building up strong cash generation.

Both ferry lines have been through two successive peak summers of very low fares and rapidly eroding profits on the Channel routes, and industry observers had seen a fairly good chance of the deal securing regulatory approval.

The MMC study is likely to address the impact of the venture plan on fares and services both with an eye to the large players in the market like Eurotunnel, and considering the role of smaller carriers like Sea Containers' unit Hoverspeed, Sally Lines, owned by Finlands Silja and Holyman of Australia, and Sea France, run by French state-owned SNCF rail.
